sentences.text: This dinosaur displayed classic sauropod traits, such as a lengthy neck, a diminutive head, a long tail, and a four-legged posture.
Estimates suggest the animal reached a total length of 16.5 meters and a mass of roughly 7.88 metric tons.
Histological research shows the animal replaced its teeth every 58 days.
Its unique tooth shape allowed it to avoid competing directly with other sauropods by occupying a different dietary niche.
Scientists propose that thinner enamel on its teeth was an adaptation for eating vegetation containing high levels of abrasive material.
Fossils were first uncovered in the Cañadón Asfalto Formation, a rock unit dating to approximately 178 million years ago, which has been re-dated to the Late Early Jurassic (Middle Toarcian) period.
José Bonaparte formally named and described the genus in 1979.
A study published in 2021 placed the animal within the family Cetiosauridae.
Phylogenetic work from 2020, 2021, and 2024 confirmed a close evolutionary link between this genus, Bagualia, Nebulasaurus, and Spinophorosaurus.

It shares characteristics with related groups like Cetiosaurus and Volkheimeria, as well as primitive forms such as Barapasaurus and Amygdalodon, and derived sauropods like Diplodocus and Camarasaurus.
Its habitat was a hypersaline and alkaline lake environment, comparable to modern Lake Magadi, situated near volcanic regions like the Chon Aike Province.
It is currently debated whether the specimen MACN CH 934 belongs to Patagosaurus, as its teeth differ significantly from those of other specimens attributed to the genus.
